title: Sync and fulfillment resilience: data-integrity and retry-safety hardening

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every terminal lifecycle command persists order state, immutable source evidence, exact fulfillment-line claims, and any available package/inventory work in one backend-owned transaction; unavailable facts create review-only evidence without inventory intent, and forced rollback plus retry cannot leave partial state or duplicate work.

Shipment, label, sync, import, webhook, manual, and marketplace callers provide shipment-scoped exact fulfillment facts or an explicit review-only unavailable result; mutable whole-order quantities never create inventory intent, and repeat settlement is a no-op.

Shopify, direct, and ShipStation label purchase use durable fail-closed intent plus immutable backend quote authorization bound to the exact order, tenant, credential account, environment, package, service, addresses, residential classification, options, and persistence facts; mismatches reject before the provider, and acknowledged, ambiguous, operator-resolved, or legacy operations cannot create a second purchase.

ShipStation confirmation retry re-reads upstream shipped truth, uses the durable provider-operation ledger for one-effect fencing and reconciliation, and leaves the marketplace notification spy at one call after simulated local-settlement loss.

Inventory recovery remains ledger-idempotent and kill-switch governed; the bounded recent production dry-run reported 672 of 672 shipped lines and 881 of 881 units represented, with zero missing orders and no apply.

The deployed exact-SHA production classification is clean: provider-pending items, recovery items, unresolved purchase intents, unresolved external operations, and unconsumed provider receipts are all zero in one aggregate-only READ ONLY transaction.

The focused quote-authorization, provider-operation, lifecycle, PS-432 resilience, Print Queue recovery/lifecycle, identity, and rate-authority suites, all 53 mandatory source-of-truth guards, strict TypeScript checks, and the 2,991-module production frontend build pass at the exact reviewed SHA.

Shipped/cancelled protections and the inventory kill switch are not weakened; closure performs no production write, label purchase or void, postage charge, marketplace notification, inventory movement, or automatic retry.

Exactly one worker owns the ShipStation stately consumers; active-job handoff, PostgreSQL connection loss, fallback ping detection, retry cancellation, bounded admission/deadlines, and idempotent shutdown reacquire or release leadership without concurrent provider work. Later PS-436 and PS-439 guards preserve the single-owner boundary while adding starvation and session-lock safety.

sotBypass.details: Terminal lifecycle truth, exact fulfillment facts, inventory movement, quote authorization, purchase intent, provider-operation reconciliation, sealed recovery facts, confirmation settlement, provider notification idempotency, and worker leadership remain in named backend owners. The ShipStation connector and operation hash consume one pure request-body owner; routes, adapters, and the frontend transport or display backend-issued intent only and own none of these decisions.

evidence.proves: The additive 0070 schema and canonical lifecycle command run against a migrated PostgreSQL-compatible fixture. Two shipments claim only their exact quantities; Shopify partial fulfillment uses fulfillment-order quantities rather than mutable order totals; the just-inserted recovery shipment is accepted while any competing outbound shipment, stale terminal status, stale writer, or injected failure rejects and rolls back. Concurrent retries preserve one append-only receipt and no duplicate inventory or package effect. Explicitly unavailable facts create review-only lifecycle evidence and no inventory outbox.

Provider-free behavioral proof covers two-worker exclusion, active-job handoff, immediate PostgreSQL onclose ownership loss, fallback ping loss detection and reacquisition ordering, retry/timer cancellation, and idempotent shutdown. One hundred foreground admission samples stayed below 500 ms with zero database connections and zero provider calls.

Real canonical owners execute against a current-schema PostgreSQL-compatible fixture: rollback removes both status and intent, retry commits one pair, concurrent duplicate intents retain one durable row, torn confirmation projections reconverge once, and repeat operations have no second effect.

A Shopify retry is blocked before a second purchase-spy call; cross-order shipment proof and no-label proof conflicting with an active shipment are rejected; a stale terminal resolver is rejected; and ShipStation retry keeps marketplace notifications at one.

Injected transaction failure, provider-ACK/local-persistence loss, torn succeeded projection, and confirmation-ACK/local-settlement loss recover without missing intent, duplicate purchase, duplicate notification, or stale overwrite.

The current backend quote authorization rejects order, client/store, credential, environment, origin, destination, package, service, weight, dimensions, residential, confirmation, insurance, and identity mismatches before the provider spy. Direct label and Print Queue callers consume the same opaque selectionRef and cannot reconstruct purchase authority.

The additive provider-operation ledger runs against a migrated PostgreSQL-compatible fixture with fake providers only. It proves the dispatch and reconciliation hash use the same provider body including residential/options, generic actors cannot mint trusted reconciliation provenance, malformed/legacy/cross-order facts stay held, exact read-only reconciliation writes one sealed receipt, two recovery workers converge on one transactional persistence/lifecycle effect, and a failed lifecycle rolls back shipment persistence while leaving the receipt recoverable. Raw-null order client identity resolves to the canonical client for shipment persistence and confirmation.

The recorded bounded production dry-run found no missing recent ledger lines/orders, while the tool defaults to dry-run and refuses unbounded --all --apply; the inventory kill switch and ledger idempotency owner remain intact.
